themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked to 6 this week versus 0.4 per week average over the prior 8 weeks—a 1500% increase (z-score: 11.62)—suggesting a coordinated posting campaign or enforcement gap in Queens Village/Cambria Heights.
evidence: 6 illegal posting complaints this week vs. 0.4 weekly average over 8-week baseline
Z-score of 11.62 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Represents the single largest spike in the district's 311 data
reporting_angles: Investigate whether illegal posters are targeting specific corridors or business districts in the neighborhood
Contact NYC Department of Sanitation to determine if staffing or enforcement protocols have changed this week

themes_detail.label: Street Signs Falling
themes_detail.summary: Dangling street sign complaints jumped to 9 this week, up 260% from a 2.5 per week average (z-score: 3.92)—a sudden deterioration in street infrastructure that creates pedestrian safety hazards.
evidence: 9 dangling street sign complaints this week vs. 2.5 weekly average over 8-week baseline
260% increase with z-score of 3.92 indicates statistically significant spike
Aligns with community board's long-standing request to 'expand code enforcement' (Agency: Department of Buildings)
reporting_angles: Photograph and map the locations of dangling signs to determine if they cluster around certain streets or intersections
Query DOT on inspection schedules and maintenance backlogs for this district—does the agency have adequate staffing?

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Deterioration Surge
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints rose to 23 this week, up 116% from a 10.6 per week average (z-score: 4.31)—a significant increase in a district where street reconstruction is a recurring community board budget request.
evidence: 23 sidewalk condition complaints this week vs. 10.6 weekly average over 8-week baseline
116% increase with z-score of 4.31 indicates high statistical significance
District has filed repeated budget requests for 'reconstruct streets' (Agency: Department of Transportation), suggesting long-standing neglect
reporting_angles: Interview residents and seniors (a focus population per budget requests for senior center upgrades) about trip hazards and accessibility issues
Investigate whether this week's spike correlates with weather events or pothole formation in the prior 1–2 weeks

themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints jumped to 8 last week, up 433% from a 1.5 per week average (z-score: 6.5)—a high-severity pest spike indicating potential sanitation or housing conditions issues.
evidence: 8 rodent complaints last week vs. 1.5 weekly average over 8-week baseline
433% increase with z-score of 6.5 indicates extremely high statistical significance
Second-largest spike in district data; suggests environmental or structural problem(s)
reporting_angles: Identify whether rodent complaints cluster in residential buildings, commercial districts, or particular blocks—map geographic concentration
Contact NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene to determine if there have been recent rat mitigation operations or identified nesting sites in the district

themes_detail.label: Tree Damage and Hazards
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage and damaged tree complaints peaked 3 weeks ago at 4 and 62 respectively (357% and 428% above baseline), alongside hazardous materials complaints, suggesting storm damage, contractor negligence, or environmental hazards affecting the district's canopy.
evidence: Damaged tree complaints: 62 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 11.8 weekly average (428% increase, z-score: 5.12)
Illegal tree damage: 4 complaints last week vs. 0.9 weekly average (357% increase, z-score: 5.21)
Hazardous materials complaints also spiked to 4 two weeks ago vs. 0.8 average (433% increase, z-score: 4.91), suggesting potential linkage
reporting_angles: Investigate whether a severe weather event 3–4 weeks ago caused the tree spike; review NYC Parks response and timeline for removal
Interview residents and property owners about whether contractors or utilities damaged trees; check DOB permits for any correlation with construction activity
